objective: Annotate function parameters, return values, and asynchronous Promise return types

stem: You want to declare a callback function type that accepts a string argument and returns no value. What happens if you define the parameter type as `(string) => void` instead of `(message: string) => void`?
options: TypeScript raises a compile-time syntax error requiring parameter names to precede colons.
TypeScript reverses the definition and treats string as the return type.
TypeScript treats string as the type and generates an anonymous positional parameter.
TypeScript treats string as the parameter name and gives it an inferred type of any.
objective: Specify function types using void, unknown, and never for callbacks, untyped inputs, and terminal error functions

stem: An API client library contains a function `crash(reason: string)` that logs a message and unconditionally throws an `Error` to stop program execution. What is the correct return type annotation for `crash`?
options: unknown, because the thrown error may be of any arbitrary type.
void, because the function does not return an explicit value.
void, because never is only permitted for infinite loops.
never, because the function never finishes execution normally.
objective: Specify function types using void, unknown, and never for callbacks, untyped inputs, and terminal error functions
